transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Patel (Redwood SE), Ethan Ross (Valencia CTO), Aisha Khan (Head of ML), Sofia Martinez (Infra), Jordan (PM)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on per-token economics, batching/caching levers, and whether Valencia should go Hosted -> Dedicated or Private. Customer has strict budget targets and regulatory constraints for residency. Agreed to follow up with pricing, benchmark plan, and deep-dive.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, I'll kick us off. Hi Liam, you there?
[00:06] Liam: Yup, hi all, Liam on the call, I'm our solutions engineer, i'll try not to break anything.
[00:10] Ethan: Hey thanks, Ethan here. We're excited, wanted to dig into cost mechanics — per token pricing, batching, caching, things that actually move the needle.
[00:18] Maya: Great, that's exactly what this call is for. Quick context, Valen- Valencia Quant, you mentioned productionizing chat assistants and a trade idea generator?
[00:26] Ethan: Yeah. Two main flows: a short-latency trading suggestion path — under 200ms p95 — and a longer analysis batch that can be slower but heavy token usage. Budget is the constraint, we're targeting $X per month but want to understand unit economics.
[00:38] Aisha: We're also evaluating data residency — some datasets are EU-only — and possible private deployment later. For now we want hosted but may want dedicated or VPC.
[00:48] Sofia: And infra is worried about spikes during market open, so burst capability and autoscale is important.
[00:53] Liam: Totally. Quick high-level: Redwood Hosted gives simple per-token pricing with shared capacity; Dedicated is reserved GPU pools with commit discounts and predictable throughput; Private/VPC is for on-prem or VPC control with additional platform fees.
[01:06] Ethan: Can you give a concrete per-token example? Like 1M tokens/day, what's the delta between hosted and dedicated?
[01:13] Maya: Sure — i'll share a concrete sheet after but, ballpark, hosted list prices are higher per token because of multi-tenant cost. Dedicated commits can reduce unit by 20-50% depending on commit size and model (and quantization). For example, a 1B-token monthly commit might drop per-token by ~30% vs hosted.
[01:28] Jordan: Is the per-token discount linear with volume?
[01:31] Liam: Not exactly linear. There are tiers and also model-specific profile. Some models are more expensive to run on GPUs; for those the marginal improvement from quantization and kernel tuning is higher. Also if you enable batching and prefix caching you get more effective lowering of cost per served token.
[01:45] Ethan: About batching — we care about latency. Our short path needs low latency, so we can't batch too aggressively. How much does batching help though?
[01:53] Liam: Batching helps primarily throughput workloads. For short critical flows, continuous batching may only be a small improvement because you prioritize immediate dispatch. For background/analysis flows, batching can reduce per-token GPU time dramatically — 2x-5x depending on sequence lengths. We also do dynamic batching where latency SLOs are honored and background requests are batched more.
[02:11] Aisha: And caching? We have a lot of similar prefixes in prompts — can you explain KV cache and prefix caching?
[02:16] Liam: Sure — Redwood supports prefix/KV caching. If multiple requests share common prompt prefixes or conversation history, the KV cache avoids recomputing transformer layers for the prefix. In practice that can cut token compute in half for some workloads. Note: transcription may write KV as K-V cash sometimes in our notes, sorry.
[02:31] Sofia: Does hosted provide cache per-tenant? We're worried about noisy neighbors flushing caches.
[02:36] Liam: Hosted has per-customer logical caches and we've built eviction policies, but Dedicated gives more control and persistent caches on reserved nodes which is more predictable under spikes.
[02:45] Ethan: Ok, so tradeoff is higher hosted price vs lower dedicated price plus predictability. Any middle ground?
[02:51] Maya: Yes — we have burst capacity on Dedicated and also hybrid routing: keep core low-volume on hosted and route heavy flows to Dedicated; or we can start hosted then convert to Dedicated when you hit commit thresholds.
[03:03] Jordan: What's the effort to switch from hosted to dedicated? Downtime?
[03:07] Liam: Minimal — same API, can pin model versions, route policy changes. We do a canary rollout and usually no customer-visible downtime. The main operational work is capacity planning and commit negotiation.
[03:16] Ethan: Let's talk numbers — hypothetical. We run a mix: 60% short queries (avg 50 tokens), 40% analysis (avg 2,000 tokens). Total 30M tokens/day. Any back-of-envelope cost?
[03:29] Liam: Back of envelope: hosted at list for large open models might be $0.00006/token for generation-heavy models (note: this varies by model), while dedicated can be $0.00003/token after commit/quantization. So 30M tokens/day * 30 days = 900M tokens/month. Multiply gives $54k/mo hosted vs $27k/mo dedicated — with big assumptions. We'll send a modeled spreadsheet with a few model variants.
[03:52] Aisha: That's a big swing — but we're also constrained by latency at p95 for the short path. If dedicated reduces latency with persistent KV caches, that's attractive. How much better latency?
[04:02] Liam: For some models and setups we've seen p95 reduced 10-40ms on top of the baseline because of decreased queuing and hot caches. Again depends on HW — A100 vs H100 and model sequence lengths.
[04:14] Ethan: Are there incremental fees for network egress or storage for caches?
[04:18] Maya: Hosted includes typical network in/out within region up to a limit; cross-region egress is extra. Dedicated contracts can include custom network terms. Cache storage isn't large compared to models, but long-term KV persistence in Private might have a small storage charge. We'll detail those in the doc.
[04:33] Sofia: Our infra is in GCP europe-west. Do you support region pinning for dedicated?
[04:38] Liam: Yes — we support region-specific Dedicated pools and Private/VPC in major cloud regions.
[04:42] Ethan: Security/regulatory: we need SOC 2, and some data must never leave EU. How do you handle encryption/KMS?
[04:49] Maya: We support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) on Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports at-rest encryption and BYOK via integrations — can share SOC2 and ISO docs. We'll attach them.
[04:58] Jordan: Competitors question: we've talked to Vendor X and also considering in-house. What's the main argument for Redwood?
[05:04] Maya: Production-first tooling, predictable economics via Dedicated and batching/caching levers, and unified API across Hosted/Dedicated/Private so migration is easier. Also observability: token-level cost breakdown.
[05:14] Aisha: For our benchmarks, we need a perf plan. Liam, you mentioned a benchmark plan?
[05:18] Liam: Yes — typical plan: you share 2 representative prompts and traffic profile; we run hosted and dedicated runs (same model family) and report latency distribution, cost per token, and effective throughput with batching/caching on. We'll need sample datasets and expected concurrency.
[05:31] Ethan: Sounds good. Our budget team needs a firm number to evaluate commit vs pay-as-you-go. Can you produce a 12-month forecast?
[05:38] Maya: Yes, we'll produce a 12-month projected spend with scenarios (hosted-only, start-hosted-then-dedicated, dedicated commit) and include sensitivity to batching and cache hit rates.
[05:47] Sofia: Any gotchas? For example, quantization impacting output quality?
[05:51] Liam: Great question. Lower-bit quantization can affect some models' accuracy; we recommend evals on your prompts. Redwood Optimize provides quality monitoring and rollback. We'll include quality regressions guidance in the doc.
[06:03] Ethan: Ok let's recap next steps.
[06:06] Maya: Recap: 1) we'll send per-token pricing and sample SOW + Dedicated commitment options; 2) Liam will send a benchmark plan and request 2 prompts/dataset; 3) Valencia to share traffic profile and budget constraints; 4) schedule technical deep-dive for infra next Wed. Anything to add?
[06:23] Ethan: No, that's good. One note — can you include a sample canary rollout and rollback plan?
[06:28] Liam: Yep, we'll add an example with rollout percentages, monitoring hooks, and automatic fallback to hosted.
[06:34] Maya: Awesome. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email with the attachments.
[06:38] Ethan: Thanks, talk soon.

End of transcript.
